items.title: How tariffs, fuel and fertilizer costs are squeezing the U.S.'s biggest apple region
items.excerpt: Washington's $9 billion industry grows more than 70% of the nation's fresh apples. Farmers are being pressed by high costs, tariffs and a strong dollar that diminishes foreign purchasing power.

items.title: The U.S. government is investigating Iranian ties to as many as 50 hacked commercial vessels
items.excerpt: The attacks, if officials who spoke to NPR are correct, may be the latest example of Iranian cyberattacks against global critical infrastructure during the war with the U.S.

items.title: Who really owns the Albanian land Jared Kushner wants to turn into a 5-star resort?
items.excerpt: Albania's Prime Minister Edi Rama has vowed that Kushner's resort project will go ahead as planned. But an ongoing investigation by Albania's state prosecutor into forged land titles could halt the project.

items.title: Jensen Huang returns to Nvidia. And, Rep. Gomez resigns amid alleged sexual misconduct
items.excerpt: President Trump took credit for negotiating Jensen Huang's return as CEO of Nvidia. And, Rep. Jimmy Gomez, D-Calif., says his resignation will be effective Dec. 1.

items.title: What should it cost to insure a home in wildfire country?
items.excerpt: Some California homeowners have spent thousands making their homes safer from wildfires. Yet all that work has barely made a dent in their insurance bills. Should they be getting a bigger break?

items.title: Doctors struggle to save babies after parents refuse vitamin K
items.excerpt: Doctors are fighting an uphill battle against disinformation about routine vitamin K shots given to newborns in the hospital. It helps prevent a rare but devastating bleeding disorder.

items.title: Black travelers on Route 66 weren't welcome at most gas stations — except this one
items.excerpt: Threatt Filling Station in Luther, Okla., was the first Black-owned gas station on Route 66. At a time when Black families needed the Green Book to find places to stay, eat, use the bathroom, it provided fuel and respite.

items.title: For workplace culture champions, Jensen Huang's return is 'unfathomable'
items.excerpt: Some who have worked to promote diversity and inclusion in Silicon Valley say Jensen Huang's reinstatement as Nvidia's CEO sends a message that all that matters is money.

items.title: The human cost of the electric vehicle boom is at the center of a lawsuit in Congo
items.excerpt: A landmark lawsuit in Congo sees 27 residents accuse a Chinese-owned copper and cobalt mine of poisoning their community and the government of failing to protect them.

items.title: Democrats probe whether Trump Jr.-aligned businesses benefit from government access
items.excerpt: Investigators say companies with ties to Donald Trump Jr's investment firm, 1789 Capital, have profited since his father's reelection.
